geometry.note: OpenStreetMap alone yields at most 'approximate'. The identification of this building as the VNS host is inferred, not stated by a source.

method: OpenStreetMap way 331249709 (building=yes, 542 m2) kept verbatim. Identified as the building that hosts the VNS only by position: it is the only OSM building that contains the trilateration solution of the NUCLEUS baselines (see geometry:chooz-vns-position); no source names or outlines the building. The two checks compare its centroid distances to the B1/B2 centroids with the VNS-to-core baselines at 15 % tolerance, because the room is not centred in the building and the centroids are not core axes.
name: Office building between the two Chooz B units (OSM), host of the derived VNS position
notes: Centroid distance to B1 79.8 m (published VNS baseline 72 m) and to B2 99.6 m (102 m).

summary.plain: An office building standing between the two Chooz B reactor units, which the NUCLEUS paper says hosts the very-near-site room. Identified by position only.
